consistency_note: No. The four landscape train clips are all underground platform shots from four different shoots: one black and white (854102), two warm-tinted with heavy motion blur and faces (2287044, 18651339), one clean 4K60 (17219505). They share an 'indoor fluorescent' look but total 45 s. Landmarks split into three incompatible looks: clear-sky daytime Brooklyn Bridge/skyline (9368738, 14306358, 14330064, about 70 s, coherent), dusk/night Brooklyn Bridge timelapses (5606317, 5606315), and Times Square (one sunny, one overcast timelapse, one shaky night). Nothing links the underground train shots visually to the outdoor landmarks.
sourcing_note: Easier than London for platform shots, impossible for POV. 'New York subway train' style queries gave four usable confirmed platform clips; naming the system (MTA, 7 train, Grand Central) produced the best one. Zero window or cab POV of New York surfaced: every train-window result was the same generic non-NYC set. No elevated-line footage (the one elevated clip is Chicago), no train on the Manhattan Bridge, no Roosevelt Island tram video (photos only). Mislabels: 'NYC subway' tagged clips were Toronto (4381133), Warsaw (7251417), Netherlands, Germany. Landmarks (Brooklyn Bridge, Times Square) are abundant. Tooling limits: ids above roughly 20 million never resolve with fetch_pexels.sh (6 of 30 attempts), two 4K files exceeded the 250 MB limit, one download (18969031) was silently truncated at 10 MiB, and two files are lower resolution than their CDN filename claims (11494571, 19332992). 30 download attempts used.
